method: Benefit links are evidence-informed, but gameWeight values and priority thresholds are invented balancing rules, not clinical effect sizes. Portions below studied amounts do not imply proven efficacy. No individual suitability assessment.

supplements.name: Creatine
supplements.portionNote: One fixed 3 g portion. A higher goal never multiplies this dose. Trials commonly use 3–5 g/day over weeks; memory evidence varies by population and dose.

benefits.claim: Supports repeated high-intensity efforts and strength-training adaptation over weeks.
Some trials/reviews suggest memory benefits; general cognitive enhancement is not established.
Cognitive task findings are mixed; this is an exploratory game link, not a proven focus treatment.
Supports rapid energy availability in muscle, not a treatment for tiredness.

supplements.name: Caffeine
supplements.portionNote: At most one 75 mg early-day portion. 25/50 mg are playable sub-portions, not established effective attention doses. EFSA attention/alertness claims concern 75 mg. Avoid bulk pure caffeine powder.

benefits.claim: Acute attention benefit; lower game portions are not a clinical efficacy claim.
Acute alertness; does not replace sleep or treat persistent fatigue.

supplements.name: L-theanine
supplements.portionNote: 100/200 mg game portions stay within amounts used in small short-term studies. No established universal safe daily upper limit, or established long-term daily benefit.

benefits.claim: Small 200 mg/day studies report some subjective sleep signals; evidence is preliminary.
A small acute trial reported working-memory/attention task signals in adults with subjective cognitive decline; not proof of general memory enhancement.
Some acute attention task signals; sustained daily effects are uncertain.
Small trials suggest stress-related signals; not an established anxiety treatment.

supplements.name: Magnesium
supplements.portionNote: 100/200 mg elemental portions are application choices, not established sleep doses. Normal nutrient function does not imply a boost in adults with adequate intake. Below both the US 350 mg and EU 250 mg supplemental limits.

benefits.claim: Small or conflicting sleep studies; general sleep benefit is not established.
Supports normal muscle function; correcting inadequate intake differs from enhancing an adequately nourished adult.
Preliminary stress-related evidence; normal nerve function is not proof of a calming effect.
Required for normal energy metabolism, not a proven fatigue treatment when intake is adequate.
